name: South Korea
targetIntake: September 2027 — Korea's Fall intake (May 2027 IB session)
tagline: A separate international track, and an academic year that starts in March
summary: Korean universities run a separate admissions track for applicants who did all their schooling outside Korea, and an IB Diploma is a normal qualification inside it: no Suneung, a small international pool, and a decision made on transcript, essays and often an interview. The Korean year starts in March, so a May 2027 IB candidate can enter in September 2027, applying on predicted grades, or in March 2028 with results in hand. Fully English-taught degrees are concentrated at Yonsei's Underwood International College, KAIST, POSTECH, UNIST, GIST and specific divisions elsewhere.
whyConsider: Yonsei's Underwood International College is a genuine full-English liberal-arts college inside a major research university: 16 majors across three divisions, roughly 3,000 students from more than 70 countries.
The international admissions track is document-and-interview based, which suits an IB student who writes well, and it is separate from the brutal domestic Suneung competition.
KAIST exempts scholarship holders from tuition for eight semesters and pays a monthly living allowance, decided from the admission application with no separate form to fill in.
KAIST teaches essentially all of its undergraduate programme in English, across science, engineering and business.
Seoul is genuinely affordable compared with Tokyo, Singapore or Hong Kong once you are out of the central districts, and student dormitories are cheap and widely available.

Underwood International College is a genuine full-English liberal-arts college inside Yonsei, a major research university — sixteen majors, about 3,000 students from more than seventy countries — and it admits for both the March and the September intake.

The international track is document-and-interview based and separate from the domestic Suneung competition, which suits a student who writes well and which makes universities reachable that are not reachable domestically.

KAIST teaches essentially its whole undergraduate programme in English, and exempts scholarship holders from tuition for eight semesters with a monthly allowance on top, decided from the admission application itself.
KAIST publishes tuition of 3,433,000 KRW a semester, which is modest for an English-taught degree.
Seoul is affordable compared with Tokyo, Singapore or Hong Kong once you are out of the central districts, and university dormitories are cheap and usually allocated with the offer.
watchOuts: The Korean academic year starts in March, and the March intake is the main one. For a May 2027 IB candidate it is not an option — you cannot matriculate in March 2027 with a diploma you sit exams for in May. The two real choices are September 2027, the smaller Fall intake, or March 2028 with results in hand.

"2027 entry" does not mean one thing in Korea, so do not read it off the top of the page and stop. Elsewhere on this site it means a European autumn start; here every date belongs to one of three different intakes — September 2027, March 2027 (already gone) and March 2028 — and the intake is named on each deadline rather than assumed. KAIST muddies even the Fall one: its own calendar calls the round the Fall Track and then says the academic year begins at the end of August 2027. Check the intake named beside a date before you plan around the date.

Every deadline that matters falls before 6 July 2027. KAIST's regular round for September 2027 closes on 14 January 2027 and decides on 25 March; Yonsei UIC's second round runs in March 2027 and decides in June. Predicted grades do all the work, and what each university does with a conditional place when results arrive is set institution by institution and is not established here.

No May 2027 IB candidate can use the 2027 Global Korea Scholarship, on either track: the round needs a graduation certificate by 31 December 2026. Plan for 2028. The Embassy Track then depends on your nationality — the 2027 list of 74 countries included the Czech Republic, Poland, Sweden and Ukraine but not Denmark, Germany or Norway — and the University Track's UIC Program is open to every nationality, but it is science and engineering at thirteen named universities, none of them Yonsei, KAIST, Seoul National or Korea University.
The 2028 round is expected to open around September 2027. Check the new country list for your nationality when it is published.

Check very carefully what 'English-taught' means at each university. Korea University and Sungkyunkwan advertise high English-medium course percentages, but that is a university-wide average, not a guarantee that your specific major runs in English for four years.

Yonsei UIC now requires proof of English from every applicant from the 2027 intake. An IB English A result counts, and so does a Medium of Instruction certificate from a school that teaches entirely in English; English B is not on the list. Other universities set their own rules — ask each one in writing.
The only official Korean tuition figure quoted here is KAIST's, and its page carries no price year. Ask each other university for its costs.

If you can claim Danish SU, it works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Confirm with su.dk before budgeting. If you cannot claim it, check whether your own country's student finance covers a degree outside Europe.

March 2027 is not available to a May 2027 IB candidate, and a page that says 'Autumn 2027' while listing March deadlines is describing two different years. September 2027 or March 2028 are the choices.

Every September 2027 decision is made before 6 July. KAIST's regular round closes 14 January 2027 and decides 25 March; Yonsei UIC's second round runs in March 2027 and decides in June. Predicted grades carry the application.

No May 2027 IB candidate can use the 2027 Global Korea Scholarship on either track: it needs a graduation certificate by 31 December 2026. Plan for 2028, when the Embassy Track depends on your nationality and the University Track's UIC Program — science and engineering at thirteen named universities, none of them the ones above — is open to every nationality.

There is no central portal and no shared calendar. Several universities run their applications on Uwayapply, a separate national platform, and several publish each round only four to six months ahead.

Yonsei UIC now requires proof of English from every applicant from the 2027 intake. IB DP English A (Language and Literature, or Literature) counts with no minimum score, and so does a Medium of Instruction certificate from a school that teaches entirely in English; English B is not listed.
The only official Korean tuition figure quoted here is KAIST's, and its page states no price year. Ask each other university for its costs.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: There is no national rule. Each university reads the IB transcript inside its own international admission track, and the category that matters is the one for applicants who completed the entire curriculum outside Korea — Seoul National University calls it 글로벌인재특별전형 II, 'those who completed the entire curriculum overseas'. None of the university pages linked from this page publishes a minimum IB point score.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No national conversion. Each university reads the IB transcript directly within its international admissions track. The Global Korea Scholarship publishes its own thresholds — 80 per cent on a 100-point scale, or the top 20 per cent of the class, or a CGPA at or above 2.64/4.0, 2.80/4.3, 2.91/4.5 or 3.23/5.0 — but says nothing about how an IB transcript is read against them.
notes: The relevant Korean category is the '12-year education completed entirely outside Korea' route, which an IB Diploma from a Danish gymnasium satisfies. This is the track that removes the Suneung from the equation.

Some universities accept the IB as proof of English, others insist on IELTS or TOEFL. Yonsei UIC lists IB DP English A (Language and Literature, or Literature) among its accepted proofs, with no minimum score.
Minimum and typical IB scores are not published on any university page linked from this page. Anything you see quoted on an agent site should be treated as unverified.
A Korean-language requirement (TOPIK) usually applies only to Korean-taught programmes, but a few English-taught degrees ask for a TOPIK level by graduation. Check the small print.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Concentrated rather than widespread. Yonsei UIC (16 majors), KAIST, POSTECH (a fully English-taught curriculum for international undergraduates since Fall 2026), UNIST and GIST, and selected divisions at Korea University, Sungkyunkwan, Ewha and Kyung Hee. No national total is given here.
language.englishProof: Set per university. Yonsei UIC requires proof of English from every applicant from the 2027 intake, and accepts an IB DP English A (Language and Literature, or Literature) result with no minimum score, a TOEFL, IELTS or CEFR certificate, or a Medium of Instruction certificate for a school curriculum taught entirely in English. UNIST asks for an English test report. Elsewhere, ask each admissions office.
notes: You do not need Korean to be admitted to an English-taught programme, but you will need it to live well, to work part-time and to do internships.
Most universities run free or heavily subsidised Korean language classes for their own international students.
The Global Korea Scholarship includes a full year of Korean language training before the degree begins — one of the reasons it is worth more than its cash value.

feeContext.summary: Korea does not charge international students a different tuition rate from Korean students at most universities, so there is no EU/non-EU split to record. Tuition is charged per semester and varies sharply by faculty, with medicine and engineering highest and humanities lowest, and the private Seoul universities considerably above the national institutes.
feeContext.typicalRange: KAIST publishes 3,433,000 KRW per semester for its undergraduate programme, with national health insurance at 458,340 KRW and on-campus housing at 664,000 KRW per semester. It is the only official Korean figure quoted here and does not apply to any other university.
feeContext.priceYear: Not stated on the source page, read 2026-09-23

sources.title: KAIST publishes tuition of 3,433,000 KRW per semester for its undergraduate programme, with national health insurance at 458,340 KRW and on-campus housing at 664,000 KRW per semester. The page does not say which academic year the figures are for.

livingContext.housing: University dormitories are the standard and by far the easiest route for a first-year international student: cheap, on campus, and usually allocated with the admission. KAIST publishes 664,000 KRW (about €430 at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026) a semester for a place. The private Seoul market needs a large jeonse or wolse deposit that is impractical to raise from Denmark, so apply for the dormitory the moment an offer arrives.
livingContext.healthcare: International students staying more than six months are enrolled in the National Health Insurance Service and pay a monthly premium — KAIST puts it at 458,340 KRW (about €295 at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026) a semester. It is compulsory, and Korean healthcare is fast and inexpensive at the point of use. A Danish EHIC does not apply.
livingContext.workRights: Students on a D-2 visa may work part-time only with permission from the immigration office, and the hour limits have in recent years been tied to Korean language proficiency and academic standing. Confirm the current limits with the Korea Immigration Service before relying on part-time earnings.
livingContext.residency: EU citizenship gives no shortcut. The university issues a Certificate of Admission, you apply for a D-2 student visa at the Korean embassy in Copenhagen with proof of funds and criminal-record and tuberculosis checks, and you register for an Alien Registration Card within 90 days of arrival — without which there is no bank account and no phone contract.
funding: The KAIST Scholarship: tuition exempt for eight semesters, 350,000 KRW a month and medical insurance, decided from the admission application with no separate form, and held on a GPA above 2.7 out of 4.3 after the first year.

The Global Korea Scholarship, from the 2028 round for a May 2027 IB graduate (2027 needs a graduation certificate by 31 December 2026). In the 2027 round it covered tuition up to 5m KRW (about €3,200 at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026) a semester, a Korean language year, airfare and 14.4m KRW (about €9,300) a year during the degree, over five to seven years. Its Embassy Track invites 74 countries and Denmark is not one.

Most Korean universities award a standing tuition reduction to admitted international students, frequently renewable on grades. Ask each admissions office for the rate before comparing sticker prices; it changes the real number materially.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

sources.title: KAIST publishes tuition of 3,433,000 KRW per semester for its undergraduate programme, with national health insurance at 458,340 KRW and on-campus housing at 664,000 KRW per semester. The page does not say which academic year the figures are for.

The KAIST Scholarship exempts an international undergraduate from tuition for eight semesters and pays 350,000 KRW a month plus medical insurance; there is no separate application, only a box to tick on the admission form, and it requires a GPA above 2.7 out of 4.3 after the first year.

A 2027 GKS undergraduate applicant must be born on or after 1 March 2002, must have graduated or be expected to graduate by 31 December 2026, and takes one year of Korean language training before four to six years of degree study, so the award runs five to seven years.

sectorLandscape.summary: Korea's Ministry of Education divides higher education into more kinds than English-language guides usually show. Alongside the four-year 대학교 that every foreigner has heard of sit 전문대학 junior colleges, national 교육대학 for primary teachers, the special-law science and technology institutes, polytechnic colleges under the labour ministry rather than this one, and open and cyber universities. An IB Diploma opens the first three of those; the junior college is rarely mentioned to foreigners and is the nearest Korean relative of the Danish erhvervsakademi.

routes.what: The route everything else is described against. Four years to a bachelor's degree, six for medicine, Korean medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and veterinary medicine. Admission for an applicant schooled entirely abroad runs through a separate international track with its own rounds, its own documents and no Suneung. This is where every English-taught undergraduate programme on this page sits.
routes.note: Divided again into national, public and private, and the difference is money: the private Seoul universities charge considerably more than the national ones and are where most of the English-medium provision is.

routes.what: Two or three years, practical, aimed at a named occupation, ending in a diploma or an associate degree rather than a bachelor's. Strong in nursing and allied health, hotel and culinary work, design, early-years teaching, automotive and mechatronics. Several run a 전공심화과정 top-up that converts the associate degree into a bachelor's.
routes.note: Rarely mentioned to foreign applicants. Whether the international track exists here in practice, and in what language, is not known; a student who needs it will not find it in the ordinary listings.

routes.what: KAIST, GIST, DGIST and UNIST: research institutes founded under their own statutes rather than the ordinary universities act, small, heavily funded, and the part of Korean higher education that teaches undergraduates in English as a matter of institutional policy. Undergraduates commonly enter without a declared major and choose after a common first year.
routes.note: They do not behave like the rest of the system. KAIST runs two international rounds. The Early round (closes 22 October 2026) starts at the end of February 2027; only the Regular round (closes 14 January 2027, results 25 March) leads to the September intake, more than seven months after it closes.

routes.what: Ten or so national institutions that exist to train primary school teachers, four years, tightly tied to the state teaching examination and to placement in Korean schools.
routes.note: Not open to you: teaching in Korean primary schools is not a path an international applicant enters through.

routes.what: Short, employment-focused technical training under the Ministry of Employment and Labour rather than the Ministry of Education. Welding, industrial automation, electrical work, machining — the trades side of post-secondary study.
routes.note: Missing from most education-ministry material because it belongs to a different ministry. Not covered on this site.

routes.englishName: cyber university and the open university
routes.what: Distance and online degree provision, including the Korea National Open University. Full bachelor's degrees, taught in Korean, designed for people already working.
routes.note: Note that the Global Korea Scholarship explicitly excludes evening, short-term, online and distance programmes, so this route is outside any government funding a foreign student might reach.

Seoul National University's academic year begins in spring, and SNU admits international students for both the spring and the fall semester.

Underwood International College admits international freshmen twice a year. Its 1st Round leads to the Spring 2027 (March) intake and closed on 22 September 2026; its 2nd Round leads to the Fall 2027 (September) intake, opens in March 2027 and announces admission in June 2027.

From the 2027 intake UIC requires every applicant to prove English proficiency. Accepted: TOEFL, IELTS, CEFR certificates, IB DP English A (Language and Literature, or Literature) or AP English, with no minimum scores; or a diploma from a country where English is the sole official language; or a Medium of Instruction certificate for a high-school curriculum taught entirely in English. The application fee is KRW 150,000 (USD 150 through the Common App).

Korea's Ministry of Education describes higher education as comprising four-year universities, universities of education, open and cyber universities, industrial colleges, junior colleges, intra-company universities and polytechnic colleges, with undergraduate programmes running two to six years.

notes: Audited 2026-09-24. Dates were read for Yonsei UIC, KAIST, Seoul National and Korea University; POSTECH and UNIST were checked for their international tracks. The other institutions are listed and their rounds unread.
Re-check in January 2027: Yonsei UIC's 2nd Round and Korea University's Fall 2027 round are both expected to be published in the spring of 2027, and neither has a day attached yet.

Not established: any published minimum IB point score at any Korean institution; how each university treats a conditional offer once results arrive on 6 July; the D-2 work-hour limits; and whether the international track reaches 전문대학 junior colleges at all.

Seoul National University's English admissions page links a Spring 2027 guideline written in Korean. Only its schedule table and the two admission-type headings were read; the eligibility text was not.

portal.name: No central portal for the international track — apply direct to each university. Study in Korea (NIIED) is the official information portal.

KAIST's other round, Early Admissions (22 September to 22 October 2026), leads to a start at the end of February 2027 and cannot be used by a May 2027 candidate.

Submitted through Uwayapply, not the university's own site, which is where people lose the deadline. This was the position on 23 September 2026.

The Embassy Track application period is 15 September 2026, 11:00 to 30 September 2026, 18:00 Korea Standard Time, applied for online through the Study in Korea website. The University Track runs September to November 2026 with each university setting its own dates, applied for directly to the university. Final scholars are announced on 7 January 2027.

The UIC Program is the only part of GKS open to every nationality: the guidelines mark its Eligible Countries as "All countries worldwide", 100 Bachelor's and Associate places across 13 named institutions, all of them science and engineering, and none of them Yonsei, KAIST, Seoul National or Korea University. Applying on more than one track voids the application. Find each university's own GKS announcement for its deadline. The track's dates are in the guidelines PDF, not on NIIED's notice page.

deadlines.notes: The alternative to September 2027, and the only Korean intake a May 2027 IB candidate can apply to holding an actual diploma. Nothing is published yet: as of 23 September 2026 the only guideline on SNU's international admissions page is "Admissions for Undergraduate, Spring 2027", with no Spring 2028 document and no "to be announced" placeholder beside it. In the 2027 cycle the equivalent rounds ran 6–9 July 2026 at Seoul National, 3–31 August 2026 at Korea University and 26 August–22 September 2026 at Yonsei UIC; those dates are not a guide to 2028's. SNU's dates are in the guideline PDF linked from its page, which is in Korean apart from the cover.

steps: From September 2026, check each target university's 'Admission for International Students' or 'Overseas Korean and Foreigner Special Admission' page — this is a different page from the domestic admissions site, and often a different subdomain.
Confirm whether your intended major genuinely runs in English for all four years, in writing, from the department rather than the marketing page.

Decide between September 2027 and March 2028. March 2027 is not available to you: it is Korea's main intake, but its rounds closed in the summer and early autumn of 2026 and it starts before you have sat your exams.
Prepare the standard international pack: IB transcript and predicted grades, a self-introduction essay, a study plan, references, proof of your and your parents' nationality, and financial evidence.

If you want the Global Korea Scholarship, plan for the 2028 round: no May 2027 IB candidate can use 2027's. Read the invited-country list first — the Embassy Track depends on your nationality, while the University Track's UIC Program is open to every nationality but covers only science and engineering at thirteen named universities. Applying on more than one track voids the application.
Once admitted, the university issues a Certificate of Admission; you apply for a D-2 student visa at the Korean embassy and register for an Alien Registration Card within 90 days of arrival.
application.selectionNotes: Selection in the international track is holistic: transcript, essays, references and usually an online interview. The international track is a separate pool from the domestic route. UIC, KAIST and SNU are selective.

tuitionEuEea.value: Korea does not differentiate by nationality — international students pay the same published tuition as Korean students at most universities.

costs.applicationFee: Charged by each university: Yonsei UIC KRW 150,000 (USD 150 through the Common App) and Seoul National University KRW 70,000 for the 2027 cycle. Check the others on each university's page.
notes: KAIST publishes tuition of 3,433,000 KRW a semester, national health insurance at 458,340 KRW and on-campus housing at 664,000 KRW, all per semester. Its page states no academic year, and these figures do not apply to any other university.

The structure to expect: tuition is charged per semester and varies sharply by faculty, with medicine and engineering highest and humanities lowest. Private universities (Yonsei, Korea, Sungkyunkwan, Ewha, Hanyang) charge considerably more than the national universities.
Most universities award an automatic partial tuition scholarship to admitted international students, often tied to grades — ask what the standing award is before comparing sticker prices.

Dormitory places are cheap and usually available to first-year international students. Off-campus renting in Korea involves a large jeonse or wolse key deposit that is difficult to raise from abroad — take the dormitory.

funding: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS), run by NIIED — the Korean government's scholarship for undergraduate degrees, and smaller than it looks from Denmark. The 2027 round covers tuition of up to 5m KRW a semester, a Korean language year costing 5.2m KRW, airfare, and an allowance of 13.56m KRW in the language year and 14.4m KRW a year during the degree, over five to seven years. No May 2027 IB graduate can use the 2027 round, on either track, because it requires a graduation certificate by 31 December 2026 — plan for 2028. Then the Embassy Track depends on your nationality (the 2027 list of 74 countries left out Denmark), and the University Track's UIC Program, science and engineering at thirteen named universities, is open to every nationality.

University international-student scholarships: most Korean universities award an automatic tuition reduction to admitted international students, frequently renewable on GPA. Ask each admissions office for the standing rate, since it changes the real price materially.

The KAIST Scholarship exempts an admitted international undergraduate from tuition for eight semesters and pays 350,000 KRW a month plus medical insurance. There is no separate application — you tick a box on the admission form — and it is held on a GPA above 2.7 out of 4.3 after the first year.
Yonsei, Korea University and SNU all operate named merit awards for high-performing international entrants. Ask each for the terms.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

funding: Part-time work is permitted on a D-2 visa with permission from the immigration office, but the hour limits and the requirement for a TOPIK level vary — confirm with Korea Immigration Service.
workRights: Students on a D-2 visa may work part-time only after obtaining permission from the immigration office, with hour limits that in recent years have been tied to Korean language proficiency (TOPIK level) and academic standing. Confirm the current limits with the Korea Immigration Service before relying on part-time earnings.
residency: EU citizenship gives no shortcut. You need a D-2 student visa, applied for at the Korean embassy in Copenhagen with the Certificate of Admission issued by your university, proof of funds, and a criminal-record and tuberculosis check. Within 90 days of arrival you register for an Alien Registration Card at the local immigration office — you cannot open a bank account or get a phone contract without it.
housing: University dormitories are the standard and by far the easiest route for a first-year international student: cheap, on campus, and allocated with the admission. The private market in Seoul requires a large up-front deposit (jeonse or wolse) that is impractical to arrange from Denmark. Apply for the dormitory the moment your offer arrives — places at Yonsei and Korea University are oversubscribed.
healthcare: International students staying more than six months are enrolled in Korea's National Health Insurance Service, with a monthly premium deducted or billed. It is compulsory and it is good — Korean healthcare is fast and inexpensive at the point of use. Your EHIC does not apply.

supplementarySteps: There is no central portal. Build a list of the universities you want and put each one's own international admission page in it, because the dates are not the same and several are announced only four to six months ahead.
Check whether the university runs its application on a shared national platform — Korea University uses Uwayapply — and make an account there early rather than on the closing day.
Ask the department, not the marketing page, whether your major genuinely runs in English for four years. A university-wide English-medium percentage is an average, not a promise about your degree.
Apply for the dormitory the moment an offer arrives. The private Seoul market needs a large up-front deposit that is impractical to arrange from Denmark.

supplementarySteps: Treat this as the deliberate alternative to September 2027 rather than as a failure. A March 2028 start means a nine-month gap after the diploma, which is close to the gap year many students in Denmark take anyway, and it puts you in the main Korean intake alongside the domestic cohort rather than in the smaller international one.

supplementarySteps: The UIC Program is the one part of GKS with no country restriction, so from 2028 this track is open whatever your passport. The 2027 round is not: its graduation-certificate deadline of 31 December 2026 applies to every track.

Read what it actually is before pinning hopes on it. UIC stands for University Industry Cooperation: science and engineering programmes with an industry placement and settlement support, at thirteen named universities. None of them is Yonsei, KAIST, Seoul National or Korea University, and there is no humanities or social science option.

Because each university runs its own submission, the first task is to find that university's own GKS announcement — the NIIED guidelines do not carry the deadline, only the three-month range it falls inside.

systems.name: Global Korea Scholarship

jurisdiction.authority: National Institute for International Education (NIIED), Ministry of Education

coverage.includes: Undergraduate and associate-degree study at the universities named in the guidelines for each track — 28 Type A and 42 Type B universities on the Embassy Track, 13 institutions on the University Track's UIC Program.
coverage.excludes: Everything else. This is a scholarship competition with its own list of universities and departments, not a general admissions portal, and being admitted to a Korean university has nothing to do with it. Evening, short-term, online and distance programmes are excluded outright, and the Embassy Track is closed to citizens of countries NIIED has not invited — Denmark among them for 2027.

choiceRules.note: Embassy Track General applicants choose up to three universities in order of preference and at least one must be a Type B (regional) university. University Track applicants choose one university and one department, and may not apply to two departments at the same university. Applying on more than one track at once voids the application.

systems.identityRequirement: An account on the Study in Korea system for the Embassy Track. The University Track is submitted to the university by its own method — in person or by post in several cases — so there is no shared account at all.

fee.note: No application fee is stated in the 2027 guidelines for either track. Universities may charge their own admission fee separately; that is not part of this.

sharedSteps: Check whether your citizenship is on the invited list for the track you want. For 2027 the Embassy Track names 74 countries and Denmark is not among them.
Read the University Information file for the track before choosing, because language scores, academic eligibility and major-specific requirements are set by each university rather than by NIIED.
Apply on one track only, for one programme only.
Expect three rounds of selection on the Embassy Track and two on the University Track.
systems.decisionModel: Three rounds on the Embassy Track: the Korean embassy screens first, NIIED screens second, and the chosen universities screen third — so a candidate can pass NIIED and still fail at every university they picked. Two rounds on the University Track: the university screens first and NIIED second.
systems.replyModel: Embassy Track candidates who pass the third round log in to the Study in Korea system to choose their final university by a stated deadline. Final scholars are announced on the same site; NIIED does not notify applicants individually, and checking is explicitly the applicant's responsibility.

additionalGuidance.title: More about studying here
additionalGuidance.text: Korea keeps a separate admissions track for applicants who did all twelve years of school abroad, and an IB Diploma fits it: no Suneung, a small international pool, and a decision on transcript, essays and often an interview. The catch is the calendar. The Korean year begins in March, and March 2027 is out of reach for a May 2027 candidate, so the real choices are September 2027 on predicted grades or March 2028 with results. English-taught degrees are concentrated at Yonsei's Underwood International College, KAIST, POSTECH, UNIST and GIST, plus specific divisions elsewhere.
